vulnerability.title: Vite server.fs.deny matcher built with picomatch matchBase lets deny globs containing directories be bypassed, exposing files such as .git/config

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.0.13 the matcher is built with slashless deny patterns rewritten to **/<pattern>, matchBase: false, nocase: true and dot: true; at the v5.0.11 snapshot only { matchBase: true } is set. static.ts is byte-identical between the two tags, so the fix is the matcher construction in server/index.ts.

severity.numeric_level_rationale: The GitHub_M CNA publishes CVSS 3.1 5.9 Medium and NVD's only metric is the same 5.9 Medium vector from security-advisories@github.com; the OSV/GHSA label is MODERATE with the same vector. No score conflict.
severity.source: GitHub_M CNA and nvd@nist.gov (NVD Secondary), both CVSS 3.1 5.9 Medium

vulnerability.category_l2: Access control: server.fs.deny uses picomatch matchBase without dot, so deny globs containing directories and dotfiles do not match requested paths

critical_operation.description: At v5.0.11 _createServer() builds the server.fs.deny matcher as picomatch(config.server.fs.deny, { matchBase: true }) with neither dot: true nor a rewrite of slashless patterns. picomatch's matchBase matches only the basename (and is documented by the advisory as buggy, micromatch/picomatch#89), so a deny pattern that contains a directory component, such as **/.git/** or /foo/**/*, does not match the requested nested path; dotfiles also fail to match without dot: true. isFileServingAllowed() in server/middlewares/static.ts:216 returns false only when _fsDenyGlob(file) matches, so an unmatched path inside server.fs.allow is served. The default deny list at index.ts:933 is slashless ('.env', '.env.*', '*.{crt,pem}'), so the bypass requires a custom fs.deny containing a pattern with directories; the advisory's reproduction sets ['**/.git/**'] and then fetches /.git/config. The 5.0 fix d2db33f rewrites patterns without '/' to **/<pattern>, sets matchBase: false, dot: true and (on top of the 5.0.12 nocase fix) nocase: true. CWE-200/CWE-284.

entry_point.description: A Vite dev server started with --host or server.host, using a custom server.fs.deny pattern that contains a directory component, receives an HTTP request for a path covered by that deny pattern (for example /.git/config when fs.deny contains **/.git/**).

source_crosscheck.notes: CNA, NVD and OSV agree on CWE-200/CWE-284, on the 5.0.0-5.0.12 affected range and on 5.0.13 as the 5.0-line fix; CNA and NVD carry the identical CVSS 3.1 5.9 Medium vector (NVD only as a Secondary metric because the record is Deferred), and OSV labels it MODERATE. The advisory documents picomatch matchBase (micromatch/picomatch#89) and the missing dot option, with **/.git/** -> /.git/config as the reproduction. Local ancestry maps the 5.0 fix to d2db33f, absent from 5.0.10/5.0.11/5.0.12 and first contained in 5.0.13; the other five commits in the advisory are the 2.9/3.2/4.5/5.1/5.2 ports.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read _createServer at v5.0.11 and confirm the matcher is built with matchBase only, without dot or a slashless-pattern rewrite, and that isFileServingAllowed treats a non-match as allowed.
An independent reviewer must confirm d2db33f is the 5.0 fix, is not an ancestor of 5.0.10/5.0.11/5.0.12 and is contained in 5.0.13.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range, the 5.0.13 fixed release and the CVSS 3.1 5.9 Medium records.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
independent_corrections_accepted: Causation separated: the directory-glob bypass of **/.git/** against /.git/config is caused by picomatch matchBase matching only the basename; the missing dot: true is a separate defect that affects dotfile basenames such as .deny. The dossier description already lists both but now records the distinction explicitly.

Precondition stated precisely: a custom server.fs.deny containing a directory pattern is required, and the dev server must be exposed over the network with --host/server.host; the default deny list is slashless and unaffected.

Deny is a blacklist on top of the allow list: a path that misses the deny glob is still subject to safeModulesPath/fs.allow. The bypass works because the default allow includes the project root; isFileServingAllowed's return-false-on-deny contract at static.ts:216 is unchanged.

Affected range is the 5.0 line only (>=5.0.0,<5.0.13); the advisory's full matrix also covers 2.7.0-2.9.17, 3.0.0-3.2.8, 4.0.0-4.5.2, 5.1.0-5.1.6 and 5.2.0-5.2.5, which this snapshot-based entry does not enumerate.

NVD is not an independent corroboration for this CVE: its CVSS is a Secondary metric sourced from security-advisories@github.com, the record is Deferred, and it carries no configurations/CPE or independent CWE analysis.
GitHub/OSV label the issue MODERATE while the CVSS base is 5.9 MEDIUM; same band, different string. The dossier records the CVSS label.
v5.0.11's { matchBase: true } line is accurate; nocase: true was added in v5.0.12 by 91641c4d for CVE-2024-23331, so the fix commit's parent line differs from the snapshot line.
review.duplicate_check: Reviewer compared CVE-2023-34092 (// bypass), CVE-2024-23331 (case-insensitive filesystem, fixed v5.0.12), CVE-2024-45811 (?import&raw) and later 2025/2026 advisories: no duplicate root cause.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No Vite dev server was started and no HTTP request was made; the bypass is established statically from the matcher configuration and the advisory.
Only the 5.0 line was diffed against v5.0.13; the 2.9/3.2/4.5/5.1/5.2 ports were not inspected.

Exploitation requires a custom server.fs.deny containing a pattern with directories and a dev server exposed with --host or server.host; the default deny list is slashless and is not affected by this specific defect.
The v5.0.11 snapshot predates the v5.0.12 nocase fix (CVE-2024-23331); both defects exist there, and this dossier isolates only the matchBase/dot directory-glob issue.
picomatch matchBase behavior is taken from the advisory and the option value, not from executing picomatch.

The reviewer notes picomatch 2.3.1's matchBase branch (regex.test(path.basename(input))) and sirv 2.0.3's dev-mode dotfile handling were read as library source to confirm reachability; neither library was executed.
Only the 5.0 line is covered by the recorded range; the advisory's 2.9/3.2/4.5/5.1/5.2 ranges are outside this snapshot-based entry.
open_questions: Whether an application's fs.allow configuration alone would already block the same paths in common deployments was not surveyed.
